hero.headline: Hegseth says naval blockade of Iran remains in place as Trump considers ceasefire extension
hero.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed Saturday that the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz is "very much still in place" while President Trump evaluates extending a ceasefire agreement with Iran that could reopen the vital shipping route.

Speaking to NewsNation, Hegseth said the ongoing closure of the strait "came up relatively often" during negotiations. The blockade has effectively shut down one of the world's most critical oil shipping corridors, disrupting global energy supplies.

Trump is weighing a potential deal that would extend the current ceasefire in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula that serves as a chokepoint for international energy markets. The blockade has contributed to rising energy prices, with gas prices climbing significantly since the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran began on February 28.

The Defense Secretary's comments reflect the administration's approach of maintaining military pressure while exploring diplomatic solutions. The blockade was implemented without a formal announcement, though U.S. Central Command indicated it would apply to any ships entering or leaving Iranian ports or coastal areas. Ships using non-Iranian ports would not face restrictions.

Economic analysts estimate the blockade costs Iran approximately $276 million daily in lost exports while disrupting $159 million in imports, representing combined monthly economic damage of around $13 billion. Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf taunted the United States about rising fuel prices, suggesting Americans would soon look back nostalgically at current gas prices.

Separately, Hegseth disputed claims that military operations against Iran have delayed a significant arms sale to Taiwan. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao previously told senators that the U.S. was postponing a $14 billion weapons deal to preserve depleted munitions stockpiles needed for Iran operations. Hegseth rejected this characterization, though he provided no specific information about the status of the Taiwan package or current ammunition levels.

Trump has made repeated claims that Iranian officials have contacted him seeking a deal, though these assertions have not been independently verified. He set conditions for any agreement, including a requirement that Iran never develop nuclear weapons.

The administration appears to be balancing competing security interests. On one side is maintaining military pressure through the blockade, and on the other is managing other Pacific security commitments like the Taiwan arms sale. Hegseth warned Saturday that the U.S. remains "more than capable" of resuming military operations if negotiations fail.

The ceasefire discussions represent a potential shift in strategy after weeks of military operations. Any agreement to reopen the strait would likely involve conditions from both sides, though specific terms have not been disclosed publicly.

cards.headline: Trump weighs decision on Iran war deal as conflict continues
cards.teaser: The Trump administration is deliberating whether to pursue a deal with Iran as the war in the Gulf enters its fourth month.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers to make a final determination on a potential Iran deal, after US and Iranian officials confirmed they had agreed on a framework for an agreement. No deal was announced following the meeting.

The ongoing conflict is already affecting households across the UK, with energy bills set to rise by £221 a year for typical users as oil markets respond to tensions in the region. The US military remains prepared to resume combat operations in the Gulf if needed, according to defense officials.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak Kills Over 245 in Democratic Republic of Congo
cards.teaser: Aid agencies are working to support health workers in Congo as an Ebola outbreak spreads through a remote gold mining town.
cards.body:
The World Health Organization has confirmed a death rate between 30% and 50% for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with more than 245 suspected deaths reported. The WHO chief arrived in the country's capital, Kinshasa, to support containment efforts against this rare strain of the virus.

Health workers in affected areas lack adequate resources to manage the surge in cases. The WHO's head called for a ceasefire among armed groups in the region to help prevent deaths from the preventable disease as aid agencies work to strengthen response efforts.

cards.headline: Former CDC director warns Ebola outbreak could become second largest in history
cards.teaser: Robert Redfield said the current Ebola outbreak could become the second-largest spread of the virus in history.
cards.body:
Robert Redfield, former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, has warned that the current Ebola outbreak could become the second-largest in history. He described it as already ranking as the third-largest outbreak of Ebola recorded globally.

The World Health Organization has also responded to the outbreak, with its chief traveling to Congo's capital, Kinshasa, to assess containment efforts. The outbreak involves a rare strain of the Ebola virus and is occurring amid challenges including regional distrust and insecurity.

cards.headline: US Defense Secretary Tells Asian Allies to Increase Defense Spending
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Hegseth said the US is not abandoning Asia but expects allies to boost their own defense capabilities.
cards.body:
At a security summit in Singapore, US Defense Secretary Hegseth reaffirmed American commitment to its Asian partners, stating the US is not withdrawing from the region. He acknowledged concerns about future arms deals and security commitments that allies have raised.

Hegseth called on Asian leaders to strengthen their military capabilities and increase defense spending. He cited what he described as "rightful alarm" over China's military expansion. His remarks adopted a measured approach to US-China relations, notably avoiding discussion of Taiwan.

cards.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump administration from immediately establishing $1.8 billion settlement fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge has temporarily barred the Trump administration from setting up a fund intended to compensate individuals who claim government targeting.
cards.body:
A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from immediately establishing an $1.8 billion settlement fund intended to address claims of government weaponization. The decision prevents the fund from being created at this time.

The proposed payout mechanism has generated concern among some Republican lawmakers and within the White House. GOP senators are exploring ways to limit or control how the money would be distributed.

cards.headline: US to seek public comment on potential Chinese tariff reductions
cards.teaser: The Trump administration will request input on which Chinese goods might be eligible for tariff cuts as part of trade negotiations.
cards.body:
The United States will invite public input on Chinese goods that could qualify for tariff reductions as the administration seeks to reshape trade relations with China. Businesses are viewing this as an opportunity to influence which products might receive relief from existing duties.

The US government plans to establish a China Board of Trade as part of efforts to negotiate a comprehensive tariff agreement with Beijing. The initiative signals progress in bilateral trade discussions between the two countries.

The World Health Organization has confirmed a death rate between 30% and 50% for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with more than 245 suspected deaths reported. cards.headline: Drone Crash Hits Romanian Apartment Building Near Ukraine Border
cards.teaser: A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war into civilian homes.
cards.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania near the Ukraine border during an overnight attack on Ukraine, injuring two people. Romanian authorities believe the drone was hit by Ukrainian air defences while over Ukraine, causing it to change course before striking the residential block.

NATO and the EU condemned Russia following the incident. The crash underscored the risks that neighboring countries face due to their proximity to the ongoing conflict.

cards.headline: Four More Miners Rescued After 10 Days Trapped in Laos Cave
cards.teaser: Rescuers freed four men from a flooded cave in Laos after more than a week underground, with two still missing.
cards.body:
Four gold miners have been rescued from a flooded cave in Laos after 10 days trapped underground. The rescue operation involved divers navigating through narrow, water-filled tunnels and sharp rocks to reach the trapped men. One miner was rescued on Friday, followed by four more, who were able to exit the cave.

Two of the seven villagers who entered the cave on May 20 searching for gold remain missing. Rescue teams continue their efforts to locate them, having drained water from the cave and worked to address collapse hazards in their search deeper into the flooded tunnels.

cards.headline: Italy Cancels Ye and Travis Scott Concerts Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Italian authorities banned concerts by Ye and Travis Scott, citing public safety and the cancellation of other West shows.
cards.body:
Local authorities in Italy canceled planned concerts by Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, and Travis Scott over security concerns. Officials said the cancellation of other West concerts had influenced their decision.

The events were canceled to ensure public order and safety, according to Italian authorities. Jewish leaders had objected to the concert by Ye, who has a history of antisemitic remarks.

cards.headline: Japan Visa Rules Force Some Foreign Business Owners to Leave
cards.teaser: New immigration policies under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are affecting foreign entrepreneurs who run curry shops and other businesses.
cards.body:
New visa rules in Japan are forcing some foreign business owners to leave the country, despite having established roots there. The changes have particularly affected curry shop owners under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration.

The immigration crackdown has caught curry shops and other foreign-owned businesses in its sweep. Some entrepreneurs who had put down roots in Japan now face departure under the tightened visa requirements.

cards.headline: US Defense Secretary Tells Asian Allies to Increase Defense Spending
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Hegseth said the US is not abandoning Asia but expects allies to boost their own defense capabilities.

At a security summit in Singapore, US Defense Secretary Hegseth reaffirmed American commitment to its Asian partners, stating the US is not withdrawing from the region. He acknowledged concerns about future arms deals and security commitments that allies have raised.

cards.headline: Reporter Describes Conditions Inside Ebola Treatment Ward
cards.teaser: A journalist walked through an Ebola ward treating adults and children during the outbreak in Congo.
cards.body:
Chief Africa correspondent Declan Walsh visited an Ebola treatment ward during a surge in the outbreak. He observed both adults and children receiving care in the facility, where a recent death from the disease had occurred.

The visit took place as the virus spread rapidly through the affected region. Medical staff were working to manage the growing number of cases and deaths in their care.

hero.headline: ICE agents to leave New Jersey detention center amid dueling protests
hero.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents have left Delaney Hall detention center in Newark, New Jersey, following a volatile overnight confrontation with demonstrators protesting conditions at the facility.

The clash occurred early Monday morning as ICE attempted to transfer Martin Alonso Soto Hernandez, a detainee who had announced a hunger and work strike on Friday. Around 1 a.m., ICE agents blocked roadways at the facility's back gate to allow vehicles to depart. Protesters confronted the agents and attempted to block the vehicles, prompting a forceful response.

According to witness accounts, ICE agents used pepper spray and batons to clear the area, pushing demonstrators onto sidewalks and into parked cars. At least one protester was pepper sprayed and another sustained a leg injury. The Department of Homeland Security said ICE "successfully dispersed approximately 70 agitators" and removed barricades before transferring Soto to the Elizabeth Contract Detention Facility.

The situation had been building since Friday when Soto announced the strike demanding the immediate release of elderly detainees, young detainees, and those with medical conditions. About 300 detainees had signed a letter alleging poor conditions and insufficient medical care at Delaney Hall. Soto's wife, Gabriela, has been organizing the protests outside the facility.

Gabriela said she witnessed guards pushing her husband into a van Sunday evening. "They were pulling and dragging him into the van," she told news outlets. "He was banging on the window. He was screaming and banging on the window."

Protesters gathered with Gabriela to block the entrance and prevent the transfer. The DHS statement characterized the demonstrators as "agitators" and said they had formed a human chain around facility entrances, set up barricades, and struck a vehicle with unidentified objects causing significant damage.

Gabriela has alleged that agents retaliated against Martin because of her advocacy work. She said guards held him in a cell for eight hours Friday and questioned him about her protest efforts.

New Jersey Senator Andy Kim and Governor Mikie Sherrill visited the facility Monday morning to meet with detainees' relatives and listen to community advocates.

"Delaney Hall must be shut down immediately," Kim said on social media. "ICE cannot be allowed to continue operating in this way."

The facility suspended visitation "out of an abundance of caution to ensure the continued safety of staff, detainees, and visitors," according to DHS. GEO Group, which operates the facility, defended its operations and said it provides around-the-clock medical care, legal services, meals, and recreational amenities to detainees.

cards.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump administration from immediately establishing $1.8 billion settlement fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge has temporarily barred the Trump administration from setting up a fund intended to compensate individuals who claim government targeting.
cards.body:
A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from immediately establishing an $1.8 billion settlement fund intended to address claims of government weaponization. The decision prevents the fund from being created at this time.

The proposed payout mechanism has generated concern among some Republican lawmakers and within the White House. GOP senators are exploring ways to limit or control how the money would be distributed.

cards.teaser: The Trump administration is deliberating whether to pursue a deal with Iran as the war in the Gulf enters its fourth month.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers to make a final determination on a potential Iran deal, after US and Iranian officials confirmed they had agreed on a framework for an agreement. No deal was announced following the meeting.

The ongoing conflict is already affecting households across the UK, with energy bills set to rise by £221 a year for typical users as oil markets respond to tensions in the region. The US military remains prepared to resume combat operations in the Gulf if needed, according to defense officials.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump to respond to fraud allegations in IRS lawsuit settlement
cards.teaser: A judge has reopened examination of a settlement between Trump and the IRS, requiring the former president to address fraud claims.
cards.body:
A federal judge ordered Trump to address what were described as grievous allegations related to a settlement that ended his IRS audits. The judge launched an inquiry into the Trump-IRS settlement that led to the creation of an anti-weaponization fund.

The settlement in question resolved a lawsuit in which Trump had demanded $10 billion from the IRS. The judge's decision to reopen the case and require a response suggests concerns about the terms or circumstances of the agreement.

cards.headline: White House releases Trump health checkup results
cards.teaser: The White House published a memo detailing the results of President Trump's latest physical examination at Walter Reed.
cards.body:
President Trump's physician released a memo following his recent medical examination, stating that the president "remains in excellent health, demonstrating strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall physical function."

The memo noted that Trump has experienced lower leg swelling and benign hand bruising. This marks the president's fourth hospital visit during his current term in office.

cards.headline: Trump endorses lieutenant governor in South Carolina Republican primary
cards.teaser: President Trump backed Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette in the South Carolina gubernatorial race, passing over other candidates.
cards.body:
Trump jumped into Republican gubernatorial primaries in South Carolina, Iowa, and Oklahoma with a series of endorsements. In South Carolina, he backed Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette in the 2026 race for governor.

The endorsement represents a snub to Representative Nancy Mace, who did not receive Trump's support. Evette secured the president's backing as the primary contest takes shape in the state.

The United States will invite public input on Chinese goods that could qualify for tariff reductions as the administration seeks to reshape trade relations with China. Businesses are viewing this as an opportunity to influence which products might receive relief from existing duties.

hero.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Test at Cape Canaveral
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night during a scheduled "hotfire" test, destroying the launchpad and throwing NASA's ambitious lunar plans into uncertainty.

The massive fireball engulfed Launch Complex 36 at Kennedy Space Center at 9pm ET, creating an orange sky visible from Fort Pierce, 185 kilometers to the south. The explosion's shockwaves were felt across Florida's space coast, with residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting shaking homes. People in South Carolina, hundreds of miles north, reported seeing a glow in the sky. Flames continued burning at the launchpad for more than two hours after the blast.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all company employees were safe and uninjured. He described it as "a very rough day" on social media and acknowledged the difficulty of developing heavy-lift launch capability. "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it," Bezos said. "We'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It's worth it."

The company called the explosion an "anomaly" but has not yet identified its cause. This static fire test was the first since the Federal Aviation Administration cleared the rocket to return to flight following a previous incident where a payload ended up in the wrong orbit during a recent flight.

The explosion has serious implications for NASA's Artemis program. Blue Origin was recently awarded a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of NASA's $20 billion lunar base. The company is also competing with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for the Artemis IV mission planned for 2028, which will mark humanity's first return to the moon since 1972.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the timeline after the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he posted. NASA said it would work with Blue Origin to support an investigation and provide updates on any impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin intends to use to launch landers to the moon for NASA, including those that will carry astronauts to the lunar surface. The explosion represents a significant setback in the company's efforts to compete with SpaceX in the commercial space industry and maintain its critical role in NASA's lunar exploration goals.

The incident comes as NASA works toward its goal of returning humans to the moon within the next two years and eventually establishing a sustained lunar presence.

cards.headline: United Flight Diverted After Passenger Attempts to Breach Cockpit
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Wisconsin after a passenger made multiple attempts to reach the cockpit.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin, after a passenger made multiple attempts to reach the cockpit. A crew member reported the incident, which prompted the emergency diversion.

The passenger was detained after the aircraft landed in Madison, forcing an unscheduled stop that disrupted the planned route between the two cities.

cards.headline: Chinese Clinical Trials Draw Attention at International Oncology Conference
cards.teaser: Clinical trials conducted in China are receiving significant attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago as the country's biotechnology industry expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Clinical trials taking place in China have become a focal point at an international oncology conference in Chicago. The attention reflects China's growing presence in drug development and biotechnology research.

China's biotechnology industry has been expanding rapidly, fueling concern among some observers that U.S. leadership in the pharmaceutical and biotech sectors may be declining. The surge in Chinese research and development represents a shift in the global landscape of drug discovery and medical innovation.

cards.headline: Stock Indexes Close at Record Highs on Technology Gains and Oil Price Decline
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all reached fresh closing records as technology stocks rose and oil prices fell.
cards.body:
Major U.S. stock indexes closed at record highs, with technology companies leading gains across the market. The S&P 500 extended its winning streak to nine consecutive weeks, while the Nasdaq gained 8% for the month of May.

Declining oil prices contributed to the positive market sentiment. Dell was among the technology companies posting strong gains. Hopes for a Middle East deal also supported investor optimism during the trading session.

cards.headline: Replimune Gets Third Chance at FDA Approval After White House Involvement
cards.teaser: Replimune will resubmit a cancer drug for FDA approval after the application was rejected twice, following what sources describe as White House intervention.
cards.body:
Replimune plans to resubmit its cancer drug for FDA approval after two previous rejections. The company received a third opportunity following what has been described as White House intervention in the regulatory process.

The FDA has agreed to prioritize review of RP1, a treatment for melanoma, a cancer that kills approximately 8,500 people annually in the United States. Replimune's stock price increased 80% following news of the productive discussions with the FDA and the opportunity to resubmit the application.

cards.headline: New York Passes Tax on High-Value Second Homes
cards.teaser: New York lawmakers approved a tax on expensive second homes, known as a pied-a-terre tax, though implementation questions remain.
cards.body:
New York has passed legislation creating a tax on pied-a-terre properties, targeting high-value second homes in the city. The tax is expected to generate revenue from wealthy property owners who maintain apartments in New York but live primarily elsewhere.

Property taxes in New York City are expected to rise as property values increase modestly. The new tax presents particular challenges for cooperative apartment buildings, and lawmakers will need to work through implementation details following the approval.

cards.headline: French Manufacturer Uses AI to Boost Worker Productivity Instead of Cutting Jobs
cards.teaser: Schneider Electric, a French multinational company, has deployed artificial intelligence in manufacturing to make workers more productive rather than replacing them.
cards.body:
Schneider Electric has implemented artificial intelligence in its manufacturing operations with the goal of increasing worker productivity rather than eliminating positions. The French multinational's approach represents an alternative to the common practice of using automation to reduce headcount.

The company's strategy focuses on using AI as a tool to enhance human capabilities in manufacturing settings. This approach contrasts with widespread concerns that artificial intelligence will lead to widespread job losses across industries.

hero.headline: Nvidia to debut first Windows PCs powered by its chips
hero.body:
Nvidia will introduce the first Windows computers running on its own processors next week, according to a report from Axios. The devices will mark the chip maker's entry into the Windows PC market, where it has traditionally supplied graphics processors rather than central processing units.

The new computers will be powered by what Nvidia and its partners are calling the N1X laptop processors. Both Microsoft and Arm have posted cryptic messages on social media ahead of the announcement, which is expected to take place at Nvidia's GTC event.

The move represents a significant shift for Nvidia, which has built its business primarily on graphics cards and, more recently, chips for artificial intelligence applications. The company now appears ready to compete directly in the market for PC processors, a space currently dominated by Intel and AMD, with recent competition from Qualcomm's Arm-based chips for Windows.

Microsoft has been working to expand Windows compatibility beyond traditional x86 processors from Intel and AMD. The company has previously partnered with Qualcomm to create Windows devices using Arm-based chips, but faced challenges with software compatibility and performance.

Nvidia's entry into this market brings a major new player with deep expertise in high-performance computing. The company has seen explosive growth in recent years thanks to demand for its AI chips, which are used to train and run large language models and other machine learning applications.

The partnership between Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm suggests the new processors will use Arm architecture rather than the x86 design used by Intel and AMD. Arm-based chips have gained popularity in mobile devices and, following Apple's successful transition to its own Arm-based processors, are seen as increasingly viable for laptop and desktop computers.

The announcement comes at a time of significant change in the PC industry, with manufacturers exploring alternatives to traditional chip designs in pursuit of better battery life, improved performance, and integration with AI features. How well Nvidia's processors perform and whether they can overcome the software compatibility challenges that have hindered previous Arm-based Windows devices remains to be seen.

cards.headline: Severed sea cucumber tissue survives for years without dying
cards.teaser: Researchers have found that amputated parts of sea cucumbers continue showing signs of life years after being removed from the animal's body.
cards.body:
Scientists studying sea cucumbers discovered that severed pieces of the animal's tissue refused to die even after several years of separation from the body. The appendages showed what researchers described as signs of immortality.

The tissue demonstrated the ability to heal itself and survive for extended periods after being detached. Researchers believe the findings could have implications for medical science and our understanding of tissue regeneration.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes rolling back coal ash monitoring standards
cards.teaser: The administration wants states to handle coal ash monitoring and enforcement, allowing them to bypass national standards.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has proposed shifting coal ash monitoring and enforcement responsibilities to individual states, allowing them to bypass current national standards.

Environmental groups have mobilized in opposition to the rollbacks. Coal ash, the residue produced from burning coal for electricity, contains heavy metals and other contaminants that can contaminate water supplies without proper management.

cards.headline: Volcanic eruption offers potential method to reduce greenhouse gas
cards.teaser: A violent volcanic eruption may have provided scientists with clues about how to tackle a powerful planet-heating gas.
cards.body:
Researchers studying the Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai volcanic eruption found that the event may offer insights into fighting climate change. The eruption appears to have revealed a new approach to addressing a potent greenhouse gas.

Scientists believe the volcanic activity provided clues that could be applied to reducing global warming. The findings suggest that studying natural catastrophic events may help develop strategies for managing heat-trapping gases in the atmosphere.

cards.headline: Google launches Gemini Spark, an AI assistant for daily task automation
cards.teaser: Google released Gemini Spark, a separate AI assistant that automates tasks like inbox summaries and local event planning.
cards.body:
Google introduced Gemini Spark, a new AI assistant designed to automate everyday tasks. The tool can summarize email inboxes and help plan local events, operating as a 24/7 assistant.

Testing shows the assistant delivers useful functionality for routine activities. However, Google created Gemini Spark as a standalone product separate from its existing AI offerings, rather than integrating it into current tools.

cards.headline: Second full moon of May visible this weekend
cards.teaser: A blue micromoon will rise this weekend, marking the second full moon of May.
cards.body:
The second full moon of May, known as a blue moon, will be visible tonight. The phenomenon occurs when two full moons happen within the same calendar month.

This particular blue moon is also a micromoon, meaning it occurs when the moon is at or near its farthest point from Earth in its orbit. The blue moon has been a source of cultural fascination for over a century, appearing frequently in popular culture and folklore.

cards.headline: Venture capitalists discuss AI investment climate
cards.teaser: Three top venture capitalists shared their views on the current surge in AI startup funding and the age of founders attracting investment.
cards.body:
Venture capitalists discussed the intensity of AI investment activity in San Francisco, with one noting that young founders building AI companies are receiving seed funding offers rapidly. The investor joked that 22-year-old AI founders in San Francisco may find term sheets in their inboxes, while 19-year-old founders might already have Series A offers because their youth signals exceptional ability.

The comments reflect the heightened competition among investors to fund AI startups. The rush to invest in artificial intelligence companies has created what some observers describe as a period of intense interest in the sector.

hero.headline: Hurricanes goaltender Andersen plays day after agent's suicide
hero.body:
Carolina Hurricanes goaltender Frederik Andersen took the ice in Game 5 against the Montreal Canadiens on Friday, one day after his agent Claude Lemieux died by suicide. The Hurricanes won the game, advancing in the playoffs.

Andersen played through the loss of Lemieux, who had represented him throughout his professional career. The goaltender's performance helped secure the victory that moved Carolina past the conference finals for the first time in years.

The Hurricanes are now heading to their first Stanley Cup Final since 2006. They will face the Vegas Golden Knights in the championship series. Oddsmakers have installed Carolina as favorites to win the Stanley Cup.

The team has not commented publicly on support measures for Andersen. Lemieux's death occurred Thursday, just hours before the critical playoff game. The Hurricanes had been trying to reach the Stanley Cup Final for nearly two decades.

Andersen has been with the Hurricanes for multiple seasons. His agent Lemieux was a former NHL player who transitioned to player representation after his playing career ended. The circumstances surrounding Lemieux's death have not been detailed beyond the confirmation that it was suicide.

The Hurricanes will now prepare for the Stanley Cup Final against Vegas. The series represents the franchise's first chance at a championship since their 2006 appearance in the final. Carolina has home ice advantage as the higher seed in the matchup.

cards.headline: Liverpool head coach Arne Slot leaves club
cards.teaser: Liverpool confirmed the departure of head coach Arne Slot with immediate effect, one year after the team won the Premier League title.
cards.body:
Liverpool have sacked head coach Arne Slot after two seasons in charge. The departure is effective immediately, coming a year after Slot led the team to a Premier League title.

Andoni Iraola is the leading contender to replace Slot as the club's next head coach.

cards.headline: Raheem Sterling arrested on suspicion of impaired driving
cards.teaser: Footballer Raheem Sterling was arrested Thursday morning on suspicion of driving while impaired by drugs.
cards.body:
Raheem Sterling was arrested on Thursday morning on suspicion of driving while unfit through drugs. The English professional footballer was taken into custody in the early hours of the day.

No further details about charges or the outcome of the arrest have been provided by authorities at this time.

cards.headline: Naomi Osaka reaches French Open fourth round for first time
cards.teaser: Four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka advanced to the fourth round at Roland Garros, where she will face top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka.
cards.body:

Naomi Osaka has reached the fourth round of the French Open for the first time in her career. The four-time Grand Slam champion secured the milestone victory at Roland Garros.

cards.headline: French Open moves advertising boards after injuries and complaints
cards.teaser: Tournament organizers relocated courtside advertising at Roland Garros following a series of player injuries and complaints.
cards.body:
French Open organizers have relocated advertising boards on the courts at Roland Garros following a series of injuries and complaints from players during the tournament.

The repositioning addresses safety concerns raised by competitors about the original placement of the boards on court.

cards.headline: NCAA warns allowing athlete who bet on own games would set league first
cards.teaser: The NCAA said it would become the first major American sports league to allow an athlete who bet on their own games to compete if a court grants an injunction for Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby.
cards.body:
The NCAA stated that allowing Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby to play would make it the first major American sports league to permit an athlete who bet on their own games to continue competing. The statement came as Sorsby seeks a district court injunction to play this season.

The organization said Sorsby's college career should be over based on its rules against athletes wagering on games in which they participate. A court decision on the injunction could force the NCAA into unprecedented territory regarding athlete gambling violations.

cards.headline: Spurs force Game 7 against Thunder in playoff series
cards.teaser: San Antonio defeated Oklahoma City in Game 6, setting up a decisive seventh game in their playoff matchup.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs beat the Oklahoma City Thunder to force a Game 7 in their playoff series. The victory came after questions about the performance of Thunder star SGA and the play of Spurs center Victor Wembanyama.

Game 7 is scheduled for Saturday. Analysts are debating which player will have the biggest impact on the deciding contest between the two Western Conference teams.

hero.headline: A24's 'Backrooms' Opens to Record $85-89 Million
hero.body:
A24's horror film Backrooms opened to between $85 million and $89 million at the box office, setting a new record for the independent studio. The psychological thriller marks the directorial debut of Kane Parsons, who gained fame through YouTube before transitioning to feature films.

The film follows a character named Mary in an atmospheric horror setting. The New York Times profiled Parsons as A24's youngest director, while Time Magazine and The Hollywood Reporter published breakdowns of the film's ending.

Backrooms is making box office history alongside another film called Obsession, which continued to perform well in its third weekend. The Hollywood Reporter noted that Obsession is also setting box office records during its extended run.

Parsons rose to prominence through his YouTube channel before catching the attention of A24. The studio has previously produced horror hits including Hereditary, Midsommar, and X, but none matched the opening weekend numbers achieved by Backrooms.

People magazine published an explainer about the film's conclusion, focusing on whether the character Mary escapes. The publication described the ending as unsettling, consistent with the film's psychological horror approach.

The record-breaking opening represents a significant milestone for A24, which has built its reputation on critically acclaimed independent films with modest budgets and targeted releases. The studio's previous box office records were considerably lower than the Backrooms debut.

Multiple outlets covered different aspects of the film's release, from its box office performance to analysis of its narrative structure and ending. The convergence of coverage from entertainment trade publications and general interest magazines indicates broad audience interest in the film.

Parsons' transition from online content creator to major studio director reflects changing pathways into the film industry. His youth and digital media background distinguish him from traditional Hollywood directors, though A24 has not disclosed his specific age in the available coverage.

cards.headline: Italy Cancels Kanye West and Travis Scott Concerts Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Italian authorities blocked scheduled concerts by Kanye West and Travis Scott, citing security issues and the cancellation of other West performances.
cards.body:
Local authorities in Italy announced they would not allow scheduled concerts by Kanye West and Travis Scott to proceed. Officials cited security concerns as the reason for blocking the performances.

The decision was influenced in part by the cancellation of other Kanye West concerts. Italian authorities referenced those prior cancellations when explaining their rationale for denying permission for the planned shows.

cards.headline: Emily Blunt Refused to Use AI in Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day'
cards.teaser: Emily Blunt said she is terrified of artificial intelligence and chose not to use it during a key scene in Steven Spielberg's upcoming sci-fi film.
cards.body:
Emily Blunt declined to rely on artificial intelligence during a pivotal sequence in Disclosure Day, the upcoming Steven Spielberg film. Blunt stated she is terrified of AI technology.

The Spielberg-directed science fiction film stars Blunt as a Kansas City television meteorologist. Her character is suddenly overcome by a mysterious extraterrestrial force while recording a weather segment during a live broadcast.

cards.headline: Charlie Puth Brings Out Busta Rhymes, Art Garfunkel, and Jimmy Fallon at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: Charlie Puth welcomed multiple guest performers to the stage during his Whatever's Clever World Tour stop at Madison Square Garden.
cards.body:
Charlie Puth brought special guests to his Madison Square Garden performance as part of his Whatever's Clever World Tour. Busta Rhymes, Art Garfunkel, and Jimmy Fallon joined him onstage for the show, along with Kirk Franklin.

The concert marked a significant moment for Puth, who told the audience that the evening made the tour worthwhile. The tour continues to additional cities beyond Madison Square Garden.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Rest of 2026 Tour to Focus on Health
cards.teaser: The Four Seasons singer announced he will take six months off from performing and may resume touring in 2027.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli canceled his remaining 2026 concerts to focus on his health. The Four Seasons singer announced he will take a six-month break from performing.

Valli stated he plans to use the time off to get well. He said he will consider resuming touring activities in 2027, though he did not commit to specific dates or venues.

cards.headline: Pete Davidson Praises Kim Kardashian in Podcast Appearance
cards.teaser: Pete Davidson called his ex-girlfriend Kim Kardashian superhuman during a podcast recording with Nikki Glaser.
cards.body:
Pete Davidson spoke positively about Kim Kardashian during a podcast with Nikki Glaser, calling her superhuman. The comments came almost four years after the couple split.

Davidson praised Kardashian's acting skills, saying she is so good. Multiple outlets covered his rare public comments about his former girlfriend, with Entertainment Weekly and E! News among those reporting on the podcast conversation.

cards.headline: Nashville Songwriters Defend Luke Bryan's New Song Against AI Accusations
cards.teaser: Chase McGill and Matt Dragstrem, who wrote Luke Bryan's Fish Hunt Golf Drink, responded to speculation that the track was created by artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Chase McGill and Matt Dragstrem defended their song Fish Hunt Golf Drink against suggestions that it was generated by artificial intelligence. The two Nashville hit writers created the track for Luke Bryan.

McGill and Dragstrem described their composition as a flesh-and-blood creation. They said the song is not rocket science but is true to who Luke is, emphasizing their human authorship of the work.

---

Note: The additional source material provided (about bird feeders, AI chip stocks, and Hannah Waddingham) covers different stories unrelated to Luke Bryan's song. Per your instructions, I'm returning the original card text unchanged since the sources don't contain confirmed facts about this story.

hero.headline: Hegseth says naval blockade of Iran remains in place as Trump considers ceasefire extension
hero.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed Saturday that the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz is "very much still in place" while President Trump evaluates extending a ceasefire agreement with Iran that could reopen the vital shipping route.

Speaking to NewsNation, Hegseth said the ongoing closure of the strait "came up relatively often" during negotiations. The blockade has effectively shut down one of the world's most critical oil shipping corridors, disrupting global energy supplies.

Trump is weighing a potential deal that would extend the current ceasefire in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula that serves as a chokepoint for international energy markets. The blockade has contributed to rising energy prices, with gas prices climbing significantly since the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran began on February 28.

The Defense Secretary's comments reflect the administration's approach of maintaining military pressure while exploring diplomatic solutions. The blockade was implemented without a formal announcement, though U.S. Central Command indicated it would apply to any ships entering or leaving Iranian ports or coastal areas. Ships using non-Iranian ports would not face restrictions.

Economic analysts estimate the blockade costs Iran approximately $276 million daily in lost exports while disrupting $159 million in imports, representing combined monthly economic damage of around $13 billion. Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf taunted the United States about rising fuel prices, suggesting Americans would soon look back nostalgically at current gas prices.

Separately, Hegseth disputed claims that military operations against Iran have delayed a significant arms sale to Taiwan. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao previously told senators that the U.S. was postponing a $14 billion weapons deal to preserve depleted munitions stockpiles needed for Iran operations. Hegseth rejected this characterization, though he provided no specific information about the status of the Taiwan package or current ammunition levels.

Trump has made repeated claims that Iranian officials have contacted him seeking a deal, though these assertions have not been independently verified. He set conditions for any agreement, including a requirement that Iran never develop nuclear weapons.

The administration appears to be balancing competing security interests. On one side is maintaining military pressure through the blockade, and on the other is managing other Pacific security commitments like the Taiwan arms sale. Hegseth warned Saturday that the U.S. remains "more than capable" of resuming military operations if negotiations fail.

The ceasefire discussions represent a potential shift in strategy after weeks of military operations. Any agreement to reopen the strait would likely involve conditions from both sides, though specific terms have not been disclosed publicly.

cards.headline: Trump signs order backing reduced childhood vaccine requirements
cards.teaser: President Trump endorsed a Health and Human Services decision to reduce the number of required vaccinations for children.
cards.body:
President Trump signed an executive order Friday endorsing the Department of Health and Human Services' decision to reduce required vaccinations for children. The HHS had already adjusted immunization requirements earlier in the year.

In the order, Trump cited his administration's commitment to protecting religious liberty and parental rights as the rationale for the move.

cards.headline: Trump attacks federal judge over Kennedy Center name and closure ruling
cards.teaser: President Trump said a federal judge should be ashamed for blocking his administration's move to add his name to the Kennedy Center.
cards.body:
A federal judge blocked the administration's effort to rename the Kennedy Center after President Trump, ruling that the arts venue is a memorial to former President John F. Kennedy. The judge also prevented the center's board from closing the facility for a planned two-year renovation period.

Trump responded with a statement saying the judge, appointed by former President Barack Obama, should be "ashamed of himself" for the ruling. The 94-page decision made clear that the Kennedy Center's name is permanently tied to the late president.

cards.headline: Former CDC director warns Ebola outbreak could become second largest in history
cards.teaser: Robert Redfield said the current Ebola outbreak could become the second-largest spread of the virus in history.
cards.body:
Robert Redfield, former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, has warned that the current Ebola outbreak could become the second-largest in history. He described it as already ranking as the third-largest outbreak of Ebola recorded globally.

The World Health Organization has also responded to the outbreak, with its chief traveling to Congo's capital, Kinshasa, to assess containment efforts. The outbreak involves a rare strain of the Ebola virus and is occurring amid challenges including regional distrust and insecurity.

cards.headline: Credit card delinquencies reach highest level since 2011
cards.teaser: More than 13 percent of credit card balances were at least 90 days past due in the first quarter.
cards.body:
More than 13 percent of credit card balances were at least 90 days past due in the first quarter of this year. This marks the highest delinquency rate since 2011.

The rising delinquency rate indicates growing financial stress among cardholders. The share of seriously overdue balances has not been this high in 15 years.

cards.headline: Bill Maher mocks Trump over low poll numbers and America 250 celebration
cards.teaser: Comedian Bill Maher criticized President Trump over his record-low approval rating and the upcoming National Mall celebration.
cards.body:
Bill Maher criticized President Trump on Friday over his falling job approval rating and the controversial America 250th birthday celebration planned for the National Mall.

Trump's approval has declined amid various controversies. The upcoming anniversary event has drawn significant criticism, with late-night hosts including Jimmy Kimmel also targeting the president's declining poll numbers and the troubled celebration plans.

cards.headline: Vibrio bacterial season arrives with risk of serious infections
cards.teaser: Some vibrio infections can lead to necrotizing fasciitis, a serious bacterial infection known as flesh-eating disease.
cards.body:
Vibrio season has begun, bringing the risk of infections that can lead to necrotizing fasciitis, a serious form of bacterial infection commonly called flesh-eating disease. The bacterial infections pose health risks during warmer months.

People who contract this serious form of vibrio infection may require intensive care or limb amputation. The infections represent a seasonal health concern.
